script.text: A US letter just reached Tehran. Is it a path to talks, or a pause before strikes?

The New York Times reports that Vice President JD Vance wrote to Mohsen Rezaei, Iran's security chief, proposing a meeting soon with Vance leading the delegation. Qatari mediators reportedly passed it on Sunday. Officials told the Times that direct talks could start next week in Qatar or Turkey.

Iran's Tasnim agency confirms it received the letter and is drafting a reply, expected around the weekend. It also says the United States has not met Iran's seven conditions for talks. The letter itself has not been published.

President Trump says the outreach was about medical supplies, and denies directing it. The Wall Street Journal had reported he did. Meanwhile Gulf states are reportedly told to prepare for possible renewed war.
Will the US and Iran meet before December? Yes or no?

upload.title: Vance Writes to Iran: Talks or Calm Before Strikes? #shorts
upload.description:
The New York Times reports that Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing a meeting soon with Vance leading a U.S. delegation; Qatari mediators reportedly delivered it on Sunday. Iran's semi-official Tasnim agency says Tehran has received the letter and is drafting a reply, and that the U.S. has not met Iran's seven conditions for talks. A response is expected around the end of the week. President Trump says the outreach was about helping with medical supplies and denies directing it; the Wall Street Journal had reported it was sent at his direction, which Reuters could not immediately verify. Separately, the U.S. has reportedly told Gulf states to prepare for possible renewed war. The full contents of the letter have not been published.
